articleHtml:
A Sonic order is not always one fixed meal.

You can choose a burger, chicken, hot dog, breakfast item, or snack, then add Tots or Groovy Fries and a drink. The drink itself may come in several sizes and can include fruit flavor, sweet cream, candy, lime, cherry, zero-sugar flavoring, or another add-in.

That means a useful Sonic nutrition calculator needs to handle both food combinations and drink customization .

Use the Sonic Drive-In Nutrition Calculator above to select the exact food, size, side, drink, and add-ins you actually order.

Sonic Nutrition Works Best as Two Connected Calculators

For food, the useful calculation is usually:

Entrée + side + sauce + drink

For Sonic drinks, it is:

Drink base + size + flavor/add-in + cream or topping

Those two systems should eventually connect into one complete meal total.

This matters because Sonic has one of the broadest beverage menus in fast food. Its current menu includes soft drinks, specialty sodas, slushes, cream slushes, iced tea, limeades, lemonades, cold brew coffee, and a new line of Refreshers.

Start With the Exact Burger Recipe

Sonic currently sells several distinct burger families rather than one generic cheeseburger.

The current national burger menu includes products such as:

Original SONIC Smasher

All-American SONIC Smasher

All-American Bacon SONIC Smasher

SONIC Cheeseburger

SuperSONIC Double Cheeseburger

Jr Double Cheeseburger

plus regional and limited-time burgers.

The recipe matters because different burgers use different patties, cheese, sauces, bacon, vegetables, and buns.

Original and All-American Smashers Are Different Burgers

SONIC's Spring 2026 national nutrition guide lists the Original SONIC Smasher Double at approximately:

600 calories

35g protein

30g carbohydrates

37g fat

1,530mg sodium .

The All-American SONIC Smasher Double is approximately:

610 calories

35g protein

32g carbohydrates

37g fat

1,650mg sodium .

The calories are close, but their recipes and sodium differ.

Keep them as separate searchable products.

Patty Count Changes the Burger Without Adding Another Bun

Current official nutrition lists the Original Smasher at approximately:

SONIC Smasher

Calories

Protein

Sodium

Original Double

35g

1,530mg

Original Triple

2,070mg

35g

670

39g

All-American Bacon Triple

860

A Triple should not be calculated by multiplying the entire Double burger.

It uses an additional patty and related ingredients inside one finished sandwich.

The Standard SONIC Cheeseburger Has Its Own Nutrition

The current national guide lists the SONIC Cheeseburger with ketchup and mayonnaise at approximately:

700 calories

30g protein

52g carbohydrates

41g fat

1,360mg sodium .

The SuperSONIC Double Cheeseburger with the same condiment configuration is approximately:

1,040 calories

50g protein

54g carbohydrates

68g fat

1,970mg sodium .

The number of patties therefore needs to remain part of the product identity.

Burger Add-Ons Can Be Calculated Separately

SONIC's official guide provides component nutrition for several burger additions.

Current examples include approximately:

American Cheese: 70 calories

Bacon: 60

Grilled Onions: 15

Hot Chili: 60

Jalapeños: 5.

These components make a true customization system possible.

If the standard burger already contains cheese or bacon, do not add it again. Only count an additional portion when the customer actually orders extra.

Tropical Heat SONIC Smasher Is Current for Summer 2026

SONIC is currently promoting the Tropical Heat SONIC Smasher as a limited-time burger.

The current recipe uses hand-smashed Angus beef, pepper jack cheese, bacon, Jalapeño Pineapple Glaze, lettuce, mayonnaise, and a potato bun. A Triple version is also currently listed.

Because this is a newer limited-time item and it is not included in the Spring 2026 national nutrition table I reviewed, NutritionSolver should not invent missing macros from another Smasher.

Use the latest official ordering nutrition when available and mark the product:

Current Limited-Time, Summer 2026 .

Chicken Needs Quantity Before Sauce

Current SONIC chicken includes Crispy Tenders, Premium Chicken Bites, Crispy Chicken Sandwich, Chicken Club TOASTER at some locations, and combo versions.

The official Spring 2026 guide publishes:

3 Crispy Tenders: approximately 260 calories and 21g protein

5 Crispy Tenders: approximately 430 calories and 35g protein

Small Premium Chicken Bites: approximately 240 calories and 13g protein

Medium Premium Chicken Bites: approximately 350 calories and 19g protein

Large Premium Chicken Bites: approximately 510 calories and 27g protein.

Piece count or serving size needs to be visible.

Crispy Chicken Sandwich Is About 520 Calories in the Spring 2026 Guide

The current national nutrition brochure lists the Crispy Chicken Sandwich at approximately:

520 calories

24g protein

52g carbohydrates

24g fat

1,470mg sodium .

If another source version gives a different total, keep the source date rather than silently combining nutrition from two recipes.

The New Tender Wraps Need Their Own Current Records

SONIC's current value menu includes:

Cheesy Baja Crispy Tender Wrap

and:

Garlic Parmesan Ranch Crispy Tender Wrap .

The Garlic Parmesan Ranch version contains a crispy chicken tender with lettuce, tomato, cheddar, Garlic Parmesan Ranch sauce, and a flour tortilla.

These are current branded products, not generic chicken wraps.

When verified nutrition becomes available through the current SONIC ordering source, add each recipe individually.

Hot Dogs and Coneys Need Exact Product Names

SONIC's current national hot dog lineup includes:

All-American Dog

Chili Cheese Coney

Footlong Quarter Pound Coney

and the Corn Dog, while Chicago and New York styles remain local items.

Current official nutrition is approximately:

All-American Hot Dog: 410 calories

Chili Cheese Coney: 470

Footlong Quarter Pound Coney: 770

Regular Hot Dog: 360.

Do not use one generic Sonic hot dog value.

Breakfast Needs Its Own Portion and Protein Logic

SONIC's official nutrition guide includes breakfast burritos, Breakfast TOASTER sandwiches, biscuit sandwiches, Croissonic sandwiches, French Toast Sticks, SuperSONIC Breakfast Burrito, and Ultimate Meat & Cheese Breakfast Burrito.

Current examples include approximately:

Bacon Breakfast Burrito: 470 calories

Sausage Breakfast Burrito: 490

Bacon Breakfast TOASTER: 470

Sausage Breakfast TOASTER: 570

SuperSONIC Breakfast Burrito: 590

Ultimate Meat & Cheese Breakfast Burrito: 820.

Keep bacon, sausage, ham, and other protein versions separate.

French Toast Sticks Need the Syrup Counted Separately

Current official nutrition lists four French Toast Sticks without syrup at approximately:

480 calories .

The syrup is a separate component.

If the customer uses syrup, add the serving rather than treating 480 calories as the complete order.

Tots and Groovy Fries Must Show Size

SONIC sides are published in multiple portions.

Current official values include:

Groovy Fries Small: 260 calories

Groovy Fries Medium: 370

Groovy Fries Large: 520

and:

Tots Small: 250

Tots Medium: 360

Tots Large: 580.

A card saying only:

Tots, 360 calories

is incomplete.

It needs:

Medium Tots, 360 calories .

Cheese and Chili Create Separate Side Recipes

Current official nutrition distinguishes:

Cheese Groovy Fries

Chili Cheese Groovy Fries

Cheese Tots

and:

Chili Cheese Tots

at several sizes.

These should remain separate from plain fries and tots.

For example, current Medium values are approximately:

Groovy Fries: 370 calories

Cheese Groovy Fries: 460

Chili Cheese Groovy Fries: 540.

The topping configuration clearly matters.

Sonic Shakes Are Size-Specific

SONIC's Hand-Mixed Classic Shakes are available in several sizes.

The Spring 2026 nutrition guide provides Mini, Small, Medium, and Large values rather than one universal shake number.

For example, Vanilla is approximately:

Mini: 370 calories

Small: 570

Medium: 710

Large: 1,040.

The serving size must be visible.

Medium Classic Shake Flavors Differ

Current Medium values include approximately:

Strawberry: 690 calories

Vanilla: 710

Chocolate: 720

Caramel: 730

Banana: 750

Hot Fudge: 780

Peanut Butter: 840.

A generic Sonic Shake value would therefore be inaccurate even when the size stays the same.

Master Shakes Need Flavor and Size Too

Current Medium Master Shake values include approximately:

Cheesecake: 750 calories

Strawberry Cheesecake: 790

OREO Chocolate: 910

OREO Cheesecake: 940

OREO Peanut Butter: 1,030.

Those same products also have Mini, Small and Large versions.

NutritionSolver should group them by:

Shake recipe → size

rather than show disconnected cards.

SONIC Blasts Need Mix-In and Size

SONIC also publishes Blast nutrition by mix-in and portion.

Examples include OREO pieces, Reese's Peanut Butter Cups, chocolate chip cookie dough, brownie pieces, HEATH, and other current or regional mix-ins.

A Blast needs:

Mix-in → Mini / Small / Medium

before the final nutrition is selected.

Slush Size Matters Even Before Flavor

The official guide states that all standard Slushes contain sugar and publishes the plain Slush base separately.

Current plain Slush base values before flavor include approximately:

Wacky Pack: 120 calories

Small: 180

Medium: 240

Large: 380

RT 44: 540.

Then the selected flavor can add additional calories and carbohydrates.

That is why Sonic drinks are especially well suited to a component calculator.

Sonic Drink Add-Ins Are Size-Specific

SONIC publishes separate add-in portions for Small, Medium, Large, RT 44 and sometimes Wacky Pack drinks.

For example, the current Cherry add-in is approximately:

Small: 10 calories

Medium: 25

Large: 35

RT 44: 45.

Strawberry, mango, peach, blue raspberry, coconut, cranberry, grape, vanilla and other flavors also use size-specific portions.

The selected drink size therefore needs to control the amount of flavor automatically.

Zero-Sugar Add-Ins Need Their Own Records

The national guide also publishes zero-sugar versions of several drink add-ins, including options such as cherry, mango, peach, raspberry and blackberry.

Do not merge:

Cherry

with:

Cherry Zero Sugar .

They are different ingredients.

“Make It Dirty” Is a Real Nutrition Addition

SONIC publishes its Make It Dirty add-in separately.

Current nutrition scales from approximately:

40 calories for Small

to:

160 calories for RT 44 , with Medium around 80 and Large around 120.

That makes it a meaningful drink customization rather than a descriptive menu label.

Sweet Cream Also Scales With Cup Size

Current Sweet Cream add-in nutrition is approximately:

Small: 40 calories

Medium: 80

Large: 130

RT 44: 170.

If someone adds Sweet Cream to a soda or other compatible drink, the calculator should use the portion tied to that drink size.

Refreshers Are a Major Current Menu Addition

SONIC's current drink menu includes four Refresher flavor families:

Watermelon Peach

Strawberry Passion Fruit

Mango Peach

Berry Citrus .

Each has still, sparkling, and frozen versions.

SONIC describes the still and sparkling Refreshers as fruit-forward drinks made with green tea and electrolytes. The frozen versions combine those flavors with a Slush-style base.

These deserve a first-class Refreshers category.

Refreshers Also Contain Caffeine

SONIC's Spring 2026 nutrition brochure states that each Refresher contains approximately 45mg of caffeine .

That means NutritionSolver should consider adding:

Caffeine (mg)

as a drink field.

This would also be useful for coffee and energy-style beverages.

Frozen Refresher Is Not the Same as the Still Version

A Watermelon Peach Refresher uses fruit puree, green tea, and electrolytes.

The Frozen version puts the flavor into a SONIC Slush-style frozen drink.

Keep:

Still

Sparkling

and:

Frozen

as distinct preparation options.

Red, White and Blue Slush Float Is Current for Summer 2026

SONIC's current limited-time menu includes the returning Red, White and Blue Slush Float , celebrating America's 250th anniversary.

The product combines:

Blue Raspberry Slush

Vanilla Soft Serve

and:

real strawberries .

It should be tagged:

Current Limited-Time, Summer 2026

rather than being mixed permanently into core Slushes.

Tropical Cream Slush Is Another Current Limited-Time Drink

SONIC's live limited-time category currently includes Tropical Cream Slush alongside Tropical Heat Smasher and summer Refreshers.

Treat it as a current seasonal product with a review date.

Limeades Need Flavor and Size

Current Sonic drinks include:

Cherry Limeade

Diet Cherry Limeade

Strawberry Limeade

Cranberry Limeade

Limeade

and:

Diet Limeade .

These should be grouped under one Limeades category while preserving each exact recipe and size.

A Diet Limeade should not inherit the same sugar profile as the standard Limeade.

Lemonades Need the Same Structure

The current national menu includes:

All Natural Lemonade

Strawberry Lemonade

Blue Raspberry Lemonade

and:

Cranberry Lemonade .

The Spring 2026 guide lists standard All-Natural Lemonade at approximately:

Small: 160 calories

Medium: 270

Large: 400

RT 44: 540.

Keep flavor and size visible.

Cold Brew Has Four Published Sizes

Current French Vanilla Cold Brew nutrition is approximately:

Small: 180 calories

Medium: 260

Large: 410

RT 44: 570.

Original Cold Brew is approximately:

Small: 170

Medium: 230

Large: 360

RT 44: 500.

Coffee should therefore have the same size-aware interface as other Sonic drinks.

Combos Should Be Built From Their Components

SONIC's current combo menu includes Smasher combos, cheeseburger combos, hot dog combos, chicken combinations, and breakfast combos.

The best calculator architecture is not to hardcode every combo as one fixed nutrition number.

Instead choose:

Entrée → side → side size → drink → drink size

and calculate the finished meal.

That becomes particularly important when the customer changes Tots to Groovy Fries or chooses a zero-calorie drink instead of a sweetened beverage.

The Current $7 Big Deal Meal Is a Perfect Example

SONIC's current $7 Big Deal Meal contains:

SONIC Cheeseburger

Small Premium Chicken Bites

Medium Drink

and:

Medium Tots or Medium Groovy Fries .

There is no single useful nutrition number until the customer chooses the side and drink.

NutritionSolver should make those selections explicit.

Kids Meals Need the Same Side and Drink Logic

The current Wacky Pack nutrition guide includes items such as:

2 Crispy Tenders

Corn Dog

Jr Burger

Jr Cheeseburger

along with Small Groovy Fries, Small Tots, milk, apple juice, and applesauce.

A kids meal should therefore be calculated as:

entrée + side + drink

instead of treating every combination as one identical meal.

Sonic Nutrition Questions

How many calories are in a Sonic Cheeseburger?+
How many calories are in an Original Sonic Smasher?+
How many calories are in Medium Sonic Tots?+
How many calories are in Medium Groovy Fries?+
How many calories are in a Sonic Vanilla Shake?+
How many calories are in 3 Sonic Chicken Tenders?+
Does Sonic have caffeinated Refreshers?+
What Sonic Refreshers are available?+

Build a Sonic Order From the Drive-In Tray Up

For food, start with the exact burger, chicken item, hot dog, breakfast item, or snack .

Then select the correct size or piece count , followed by any supported additions or sauces.

Choose Tots, Groovy Fries, or another side and its actual size.

For drinks, select:

drink family → exact flavor → Wacky Pack/Small/Medium/Large/RT 44 where available → add-ins → cream/toppings .

Finally, add any shake, Blast, dessert, or extra snack consumed with the meal.

Sonic's food menu is broad, but its drink customization is what makes the restaurant especially different from most burger chains. A calculator that understands both systems can answer the actual order much more accurately than hundreds of disconnected nutrition cards.
